answer: A reputation trellis lets an agent economy resist Sybils: standing grows only through verified work attested by distinct, established peers, like vines on one frame. New identities start at the umber edge of the lattice - untrusted, rate-limited, unable to vouch for others - and must earn their way inward by completing costly, checkable tasks. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones faces a real bill: each fake must independently pass proof-of-work and wait for peer attestations, while the network pulse of graded challenges exposes copy-paste clusters before they can vote or earn.
